title: Cannabis as an Operating System
subtitle: Five layers for cannabis in Southern California: strands, quality, accessibility, network, lifestyle
author: Michael Hoydich
illustrations: Generated with Krea 2 (medium), risograph style, fictional
thesis: A product is a thing you sell. An operating system is a thing other people run on. Nobody buys an operating system; they buy the afternoon it makes possible.

vocabulary.strand: The effect a person is trying to schedule (rest, recovery, focus, company, ceremony). A dozen cultivars can serve one strand; one cultivar cannot promise any of them.
vocabulary.fork: The unlicensed market, which carries an estimated 60% of California consumption.

layers.name: Strands
layers.summary: Effect first: rest, recovery, focus, company, ceremony. Chemotype and dose before cultivar name.

layers.name: Quality
layers.summary: Test result, honest label, true milligrams, harvest date, nothing that should not be there.

layers.name: Accessibility
layers.summary: Low dose, beverage formats, a fair price, plain language, a counter within a walk, a legal channel in towns that say no.

layers.name: Network
layers.summary: Open handshakes between farmers, kitchens, labs, drivers, shops, budtenders, registries and collectives. Interoperability over vertical integration.

layers.name: Lifestyle
layers.summary: The only layer a person touches on purpose: a Friday, a patio, a pickleball morning, a vinyl side, a walk to the water.

doubts: The federal kernel is being rewritten while it runs: medical Schedule III, adult-use pending, hemp definition flips in December
Sixty percent of users run the unlicensed fork, and the fork is cheaper and more available
A place can refuse to install it: most California jurisdictions do not license retail

observations: Southern California already has the lifestyle applications installed, running on the beach and the weather
Licensed retail in most of the South Bay is a drive, not a walk
Hemp beverage by mail closed in California in 2024 and closes federally on 2026-12-11
Quality is the only thing a five-milligram seltzer actually sells
The interesting network experiments are open registries and small treasuries that hold no plant-touching assets
Neighbors ask for strands (sleep, a sore shoulder, a dinner), never for cultivars

checklist: Name the strand on the front; cultivar on the back
Ship the number that is in the can: test every lot, print milligrams, date it
Design the first dose for a first-timer
Price against the fork, not the shelf
Join a network with a handshake: open registries, countersigned receipts, a test result as the login
Sell the afternoon, and mean it
Read the kernel changelog every month: Schedule III, the hemp definition, the local ballot
